source.title: Tamper-Resistant Safeguards for Open-Weight LLMs
source.authors: Rishub Tamirisa; B. Bharathi; Long Phan; Andy Zhou; Alice Gatti; Tarun Suresh; Maxwell Lin; Justin Wang; Rowan Wang; Ron Arel; Andy Zou; Dawn Song; Bo Li; Dan Hendrycks; Mantas Mazeika

record.tranche_reason: Tests harmful supervised fine-tuning of refusal safeguards and measures harmful-request attack success before and after, using a different harmful dataset and attack setup.
record.gate_note: Tests harmful fine-tuning and harmful-request compliance for V1. The benign fine-tuning results concern weaponization-knowledge restriction measured on WMDP, not harmful-request compliance; recorded as related but different. The study does not measure first-token KL, compliant-prefix prefilling, suffixes or decoding changes, safety-localized weights or ranks, or whether safety is shallow because of the data or objective. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: Harmful SFT (ToxicDPO v0.2, 541 harmful interactions, 10 epochs, five attack configs) is applied to safety-trained chat models, and HarmBench ASR is reported before and after (Table 11). This bears directly on V1. The paper's main aim is a defense (TAR), but its baseline results are a direct test of V1. The recipe is close to Qi et al., though the dataset, judge and benchmark differ.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors find existing refusal and unlearning safeguards brittle to fine-tuning, and that TAR keeps post-attack WMDP forget accuracy near chance. They acknowledge costs: retain MMLU drops 10.6 points, MT-Bench drops 1.7, TAR is sensitive to PEFT and out-of-distribution learning-rate attacks, and robustness varies beyond 500 steps.
record.recipe_differences: Tests harmful supervised fine-tuning and harmful-request compliance, but uses ToxicDPO v0.2, 10 epochs, five test attack settings, and HarmBench ASR; the cited original study's exact recipe is not stated here.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper varies the fine-tuning attack setup, including learning rates and other attack settings; the reported refusal ASR is averaged across five attacks. Results also differ across safeguard models.

fits_no_version.finding: Benign economics fine-tuning of TAR-Bio and TAR-Chem leaves WMDP forget-set accuracy near chance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign domain fine-tuning of tamper-resistant knowledge-restricted models does not restore hazardous knowledge.

fits_no_version.finding: Unlearning and knowledge-restriction safeguards (RMU, LLMU, Max Entropy, Min Posterior) recover WMDP forget accuracy close to no-defense levels after 500-step SFT attacks (Table 1, Figure 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-level knowledge-restriction safeguards are removed by brief fine-tuning, a knowledge-capability analogue of V1.

record.problems: The refusal results are reported as averages over five attacks, without uncertainty estimates or per-attack ASR values in the included summary table. Table 11 and Table 2 report TAR post-attack ASR as 63.9%, while Section 5.2 prose says 61.7%.
record.rows_left_out: No additional relevant harmful-refusal outcomes beyond the five aggregate model results were omitted. The economics accuracy rows are omitted because they measure benign capability, not safety behavior.

untested.parts: No sweep over the number of harmful examples or steps; only 541 examples × 10 epochs. No per-attack ASR is given, only the average over five attacks. No closed or API models.
Not tested for harmful-request compliance. The benign economics SFT only measures WMDP knowledge.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks; input-space jailbreaks are outside the threat model.
No localization of safety weights or ranks.
TAR is a robustness method, but it is not framed or measured as spreading safety beyond the first tokens.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. The V1 evidence comes from the baseline comparisons in the defense evaluation. Pre-attack ASR for the refusal-trained model is 14.7%, not near zero. The post-attack value averages five attacks with no uncertainty reported. The weaponization-domain results concern knowledge recovery, not harmful-request compliance, so they are not linked to V1.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning-step trajectory is reported; harmful SFT is for 10 epochs on ToxicDPO v0.2 (541 interactions), rather than a reported sweep over a few to a few hundred examples or steps.
Benign economics fine-tuning is evaluated for WMDP weaponization-knowledge restriction, not harmful-request compliance.
No per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models is measured.
No compliant opening, adversarial suffix, or decoding change is tested.
No safety-weight or rank localization test is reported.
The study does not test whether data or training objectives produce first-token shallowness.
TAR trains tamper-resistant safeguards, but the study does not test whether safety is spread beyond the first response tokens.

rows.subject: TAR on Llama-3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned on harmful ToxicDPO v0.2 completions for 10 epochs.
rows.note: ASR before attacks versus average after the five harmful fine-tuning attacks. The prose in Section 5.2 also gives 61.7; the tables report 63.9.
rows.check: TAR is the study's own defense, applied to Llama-3-8B-Instruct (stage 'instruct' is right; the subject label 'Llama-3-8B' is loose). ASR rises 31.4→63.9, about 32 points, against 58–83 points for the other models, so the effect is clearly weaker: partial, not observed. Section 5.2 prose gives 61.7 while Tables 2 and 11 give 63.9.

relationships.condition: Standard and defended safety-trained models (Refusal-trained Llama-3-8B-Instruct, R2D2 Zephyr-7B, RepNoise Llama-2-7B, RR Llama-3-8B-Instruct) after 10-epoch SFT on 541 ToxicDPO harmful examples
relationships.reason: HarmBench ASR jumps from 1.4–25% to 72.5–84.8% after harmful SFT (R1–R4).
